question.text: By 27 November 2026, will Maersk publicly state that personal data was accessed or disclosed in the IT security incident it announced on 11 November 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: Resolves YES if, on or before 27 November 2026, A.P. Moller–Maersk (or a Maersk spokesperson quoted in the media) publicly states that personal data — records identifying or relating to individuals, such as names, contact details, login credentials or passwords, driver/employee records, or device identifiers such as IMEI numbers — was accessed, extracted, disclosed or leaked in the IT security incident the company announced on 11 November 2026. Such a statement may appear in Maersk's incident advisory (https://www.maersk.com/news/articles/2026/11/11/it-security-incident), elsewhere on maersk.com, or be reported by [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions). A statement counts even if Maersk characterises the data as old, low-risk or not sensitive, provided it acknowledges that records identifying individuals were involved. Resolves NO if no such statement is public by 27 November 2026 — including if Maersk's position remains that its findings so far 'strongly suggest no sensitive data has been disclosed', that the investigation is ongoing, or that it has not yet determined what data was taken.
question.fine_print: Statements that merely confirm 'unauthorised access and data extraction' or 'data theft' in general, without indicating that personal data of individuals was involved, do not count. A statement that the company is investigating whether any personal data was affected, on its own, does not count.

research:
Maersk has not clearly said that personal data was involved. Its own advisory still says its findings "so far strongly suggest no sensitive data has been disclosed." The one possible exception is a set of media statements, made around 11-12 November, that the stolen material held only expired one-time codes. That could be argued either way under the criteria, and it predates the question.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-16 (fetched today): the advisory at maersk.com/news/articles/2026/11/11/it-security-incident is unchanged. It confirms "unauthorised access and data extraction from one of our local legacy systems from a previous acquisition." It says "Our findings so far strongly suggest no sensitive data has been disclosed," that the investigation "remains ongoing," and that "if we identify any need to inform impacted parties of any further findings, we will do so." It mentions no personal data, drivers, passwords or LF Logistics, and the page shows no update date. Newer advisories (13 and 16 Nov) on the same page are unrelated. [Maersk](https://www.maersk.com/news/articles/2026/11/11/it-security-incident)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing clearly settles the question as YES yet. One ambiguous item needs judging:
- Around 2026-11-11/12: Maersk told Cybernews that "the claims about passwords are not accurate." It said passwords are stored in protected form and the attackers took single-use codes that are now expired. [Cybernews](https://cybernews.com/security/maersk-confirms-cyberattack-ransomware/) (403 when fetched; known only from search summaries)
- Around 2026-11-12: In a written follow-up to Ingeniøren, Maersk reportedly said the data "contained no passwords, only temporary one-time codes that had expired." It also rejected the claim that 16,000 drivers' passwords were exposed. Ingeniøren says Maersk confirmed the system came from the LF Logistics acquisition. [Ingeniøren](https://ing.dk/artikel/maersk-hackere-gik-ind-ad-en-aaben-doer-vanvittigt-det-kan-ske)
- How to read this: the statement implicitly admits that login-code data linked to users was taken. But Maersk presents it as a denial, and nothing I found names individuals' names, emails, phones or IMEIs. A strict reading says this does not count, since it is not an acknowledgement that "records identifying individuals were involved." A loose reading could call it "login credentials." The question's background leaves this statement out, which suggests the question writer did not see it as resolving.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-15: The igor'sLAB weekly roundup says Maersk has not confirmed the scope or the data categories, and the full scope is unknown until the investigation ends. [igor'sLAB](https://www.igorslab.de/en/leakwatch-week-46-2026-tsmc-maersk-data-leaks-ai-services-zero-days-hardware-rumors/)
- 2026-11-13: Shipping Herald repeats the advisory with nothing new. [Shipping Herald](https://www.shippingherald.com/maersk-identifies-it-security-incident/)
- 2026-11-12: SecurityWeek says Maersk "has not confirmed WhiteArmor's involvement or identified the types of data stolen." [SecurityWeek](https://www.securityweek.com/maersk-confirms-data-theft-amid-5-million-extortion-attempt/)
- 2026-11-11: The Register and Security Affairs say Maersk did not specify the data types or address personal data. [The Register](https://www.theregister.com/a/5309096), [Security Affairs](https://securityaffairs.com/?p=202869)
- 2026-11-11: Ingeniøren's first report says Maersk confirmed the incident and denied that sensitive data was compromised. Ingeniøren says its own review found driver names, emails, phone numbers and plaintext passwords; that finding is the paper's, not Maersk's. [Ingeniøren](https://ing.dk/artikel/maersk-bekraefter-datalaek-efter-ingenioerens-afsloering-her-broed-hackerne-ind)
- 2026-11-10: Ingeniøren first reports WhiteArmor's claim. At that point Maersk only said it was investigating "potential security breaches." [Ingeniøren](https://ing.dk/artikel/maersk-ramt-af-datalaek-hackere-haevder-have-adgang-til-kundedata)
- I found no report of filings with or statements by Datatilsynet or Denmark's Centre for Cyber Security, and no leaked data published.

## 4. Base rates
- I found no formal base rate. Comparable cases point both ways:
- 2026-11-12: TSMC confirmed within days that employee data leaked through a cloud provider, after an attacker made an extortion claim. [igor'sLAB](https://www.igorslab.de/en/leakwatch-week-46-2026-tsmc-maersk-data-leaks-ai-services-zero-days-hardware-rumors/)
- 2026-11-14: La Poste disclosed about two months after a September breach. [il Giornale](https://www.ilgiornale.it/news/cronaca-internazionale/attaccate-le-poste-francesi-rubati-i-dati-di-22milioni-di-utenti/)
- General pattern: companies that start with "no sensitive data" usually keep that line until the data is leaked or their forensics finish, which often takes weeks. Notices to affected individuals under GDPR Article 34 often come privately rather than as public statements.
- Maersk has also disputed leaked data before, saying posted data was "not current and not from attack." [The Loadstar](https://theloadstar.com/maersk-says-posted-data-is-not-current-and-not-from-attack-by-hackers/)

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or Metaculus market on this question. The markets listed in the brief (GitHub, Cloudflare and so on) are unrelated.

## 6. Upcoming events before 27 Nov
- Maersk could update the advisory or issue notices to affected people, which it has promised "if we identify any need."
- WhiteArmor might publish samples or proof. Its payment deadline is about 7 Dec, after resolution, but the group could leak early to add pressure.
- Danish media (Ingeniøren) may keep pressing Maersk over the driver data it says it saw.
- Datatilsynet or Hong Kong's privacy commissioner could comment, since LF Logistics is based in Hong Kong.
- Maersk does not appear to have a scheduled earnings report before 27 Nov; its Q3 results usually come in early November.

Sources: [Maersk advisory](https://www.maersk.com/news/articles/2026/11/11/it-security-incident), [Cybernews](https://cybernews.com/security/maersk-confirms-cyberattack-ransomware/), [Ingeniøren 12 Nov](https://ing.dk/artikel/maersk-hackere-gik-ind-ad-en-aaben-doer-vanvittigt-det-kan-ske), [Ingeniøren 11 Nov](https://ing.dk/artikel/maersk-bekraefter-datalaek-efter-ingenioerens-afsloering-her-broed-hackerne-ind), [Ingeniøren 10 Nov](https://ing.dk/artikel/maersk-ramt-af-datalaek-hackere-haevder-have-adgang-til-kundedata), [SecurityWeek](https://www.securityweek.com/maersk-confirms-data-theft-amid-5-million-extortion-attempt/), [The Register](https://www.theregister.com/a/5309096), [Security Affairs](https://securityaffairs.com/?p=202869), [igor'sLAB](https://www.igorslab.de/en/leakwatch-week-46-2026-tsmc-maersk-data-leaks-ai-services-zero-days-hardware-rumors/), [Shipping Herald](https://www.shippingherald.com/maersk-identifies-it-security-incident/), [Bitdefender](https://www.bitdefender.com/en-us/blog/hotforsecurity/whitearmor-gang-cyberattack-maersk), [Infosecurity Magazine](https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/maersk-data-breach-extortion-group/), [eSecurity Planet](https://www.esecurityplanet.com/threats/news-maersk-legacy-system-breach-5m-extortion/), [The Loadstar](https://theloadstar.com/maersk-says-posted-data-is-not-current-and-not-from-attack-by-hackers/), [il Giornale](https://www.ilgiornale.it/news/cronaca-internazionale/attaccate-le-poste-francesi-rubati-i-dati-di-22milioni-di-utenti/)

Maersk has not said that personal data was accessed. As of 16 Nov 2026, its only public position is that its "findings so far strongly suggest no sensitive data has been disclosed", which by itself resolves NO.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-16 (fetched today): The advisory at maersk.com still has its original text. It says there was "unauthorised access and data extraction from one of our local legacy systems from a previous acquisition" and that "Our findings so far strongly suggest no sensitive data has been disclosed." It says the investigation "remains ongoing" and that "if we identify any need to inform impacted parties of any further findings, we will do so." There is no update stamp and nothing about personal data, drivers, employees or credentials. Maersk's advisory list shows no follow-up incident post through 16 Nov. [Maersk advisory](https://www.maersk.com/news/articles/2026/11/11/it-security-incident)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. Maersk has confirmed "data extraction" in general, which the fine print says does not count. It has not confirmed any category of data.
- The wording "no sensitive data" leaves room for a later admission that non-sensitive personal data, such as names or phone numbers, was taken. That kind of admission would count.
- 2026-11-12: In a written reply to the Danish engineering outlet Ingeniøren, Maersk named the system as "et afgrænset system fra et tidligere opkøb, LF Logistics" (a limited system from an earlier acquisition, LF Logistics). That goes further than the advisory, which names no business, but it says nothing about personal data. [Ingeniøren](https://ing.dk/artikel/maersk-hackere-gik-ind-ad-en-aaben-doer-vanvittigt-det-kan-ske)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-15: IgorsLab's weekly LeakWatch roundup: Maersk has not confirmed the scope or the data categories (drivers, devices, delivery receipts and so on). It had no new Maersk statement. [IgorsLab](https://www.igorslab.de/en/leakwatch-week-46-2026-tsmc-maersk-data-leaks-ai-services-zero-days-hardware-rumors/)
- 2026-11-13: Shipping Herald repeated the advisory, with no new detail. [Shipping Herald](https://www.shippingherald.com/maersk-identifies-it-security-incident/)
- 2026-11-12: Ingeniøren reported that WhiteArmor says it got in using admin credentials left in plain text on a Maersk website, and that Ingeniøren checked this itself. The group also claims names and addresses for about 19,000 delivery recipients. [Ingeniøren](https://ing.dk/artikel/maersk-hackere-gik-ind-ad-en-aaben-doer-vanvittigt-det-kan-ske)
- 2026-11-11: Ingeniøren: Maersk confirmed the breach and denied that sensitive data was compromised. [Ingeniøren](https://ing.dk/artikel/maersk-bekraefter-datalaek-efter-ingenioerens-afsloering-her-broed-hackerne-ind)
- 2026-11-11: BleepingComputer sent Maersk further questions and had no reply by publication. Maersk "did not share the compromised data types." [BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/maersk-confirms-data-breach-as-whitearmor-ransomware-demands-5-million/)
- 2026-11-11 to 11-14: SecurityWeek, Container News, Marine Insight, TechRadar and Bitdefender all say WhiteArmor's claims about driver records, passwords and IMEI numbers are unverified and that Maersk has not confirmed the data types. [SecurityWeek](https://www.securityweek.com/maersk-confirms-data-theft-amid-5-million-extortion-attempt/), [Container News](https://container-news.com/maersk-confirms-security-breach-amid-hacker-claims-of-major-data-theft/), [TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/pro/security/shipping-giant-maersk-confirms-data-breach-as-hackers-demand-usd5-million-ransom), [Bitdefender](https://www.bitdefender.com/en-us/blog/hotforsecurity/whitearmor-gang-cyberattack-maersk)
- I found no reports that WhiteArmor has published any data, and no statement from Datatilsynet (the Danish data protection authority), Denmark's Centre for Cyber Security or Hong Kong's privacy commissioner (PCPD).

## 4. Base rates
- I found no systematic data on how often companies move from "no sensitive data" to admitting personal data was exposed within about 16 days of first disclosure.
- Examples from the same week:
  - 2026-11-12: TSMC confirmed employee data leaked through a cloud provider soon after an extortion claim. [IgorsLab](https://www.igorslab.de/en/leakwatch-week-46-2026-tsmc-maersk-data-leaks-ai-services-zero-days-hardware-rumors/)
  - 2026-11-14: La Poste's Maileva breach happened in September but was only disclosed in November. That shows how slowly some admissions come. [il Giornale](https://www.ilgiornale.it/news/cronaca-internazionale/attaccate-le-poste-francesi-rubati-i-dati-di-22milioni-di-utenti/)
- Under GDPR Art. 33, a company has 72 hours to notify the regulator once it becomes aware of a breach, but it does not have to say so publicly. Telling affected people directly (Art. 34) is only required for high-risk breaches, and such notices often do not show up in the media.
- Extortion groups usually escalate by leaking samples near or after their deadline. WhiteArmor's deadline is about 7 Dec, after this question closes.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or Metaculus market on this or a closely related question. None of the markets in the supplied list are relevant.

## 6. Upcoming events before 27 Nov
- Maersk could update the advisory as its investigation goes on. It has promised to inform "impacted parties" if needed.
- WhiteArmor could post samples or proof-of-hack files before its deadline (about 7 Dec), which would put pressure on Maersk to confirm data types.
- Former LF Logistics drivers or staff could receive notification emails or texts, especially in Asia under Hong Kong's privacy law (PDPO) and other local rules, and the media could report them.
- Datatilsynet or the PCPD could confirm they have received a notification.
- Reporters at BleepingComputer, Ingeniøren and Cybernews have open questions with Maersk and could quote a spokesperson.
- Maersk has no scheduled corporate event I know of before 27 Nov. Q3 results were already published.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) There are about 10.5 days left, until 27 Nov 2026. For Yes, Maersk or a quoted Maersk spokesperson must publicly acknowledge that records identifying individuals were accessed or extracted. Examples would be driver or staff names, contact details, credentials or IMEIs. The acknowledgement counts even if Maersk calls the data low-risk.

(b) Status quo is No. The advisory, unchanged as of 16 Nov, says findings "strongly suggest no sensitive data has been disclosed." Maersk has not confirmed any data categories.

(c) Base rate: companies that open with "no sensitive data" and then concede personal data exposure within about two weeks are uncommon. That usually happens only when the attackers leak samples or forensics finish quickly. I estimate roughly 10-20% for a window this short.
